newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai central bank denies offshore baht rumour.
newsitem.headline: Thai central bank denies offshore baht rumour.

text.p: The Bank of Thailand (BOT) on Friday denied rumours, mainly from Singapore, that the baht may be devalued and stressed such a move was not part of any plans the central bank may have for the currency.
"I just received a report about the rumour in Singapore. I want to stress that baht devaluation is not in any way planned by the bank, BOT spokeswoman Kleo-thong Hetrakul told Reuters.
The baht fell sharply to 25.340-25.345 to the dollar at midday from 25.334-25.337 in early morning trade on heavy dollar buying against the baht by offshore players, dealers said.
The one-month dollar-baht swap premium, however, rose to 10.0-11.0 satang at midday from 9.0-9.5 satang earlier this morning.
"There was heavy baht selling for the dollar near lunch break by players in Singapore," said one senior dealer at a local bank."
"They usually attack the baht during the lunch break here and after the Bank of Thailand's dollar market operation with domestic commercial banks was closed," she said.
"These are all self-serving rumours from Singapore. I know, I used to work there," said the treasury manager of a foreign bank.
Rumours that the Thai baht and the Indonesian rupiah may be devalued were triggered by Singapore players, they added.

Dealers in Singapore said Thailand's looming political crisis, the downgrade of short-term currency debt rating by Moody's and market talk of financial defaults at Thai brokerage houses had made the baht vulnerable.
